main_text.l: Quatuor: primo, si judex litem suam fecerit:
non proprie ex maleficio obligatus videtur:
sed quia neq; ex maleficio, neq; ex contractu obliga-
tus est, & utiq; peccasse aliquid intelligitur, licet per
imprudentiam: ideo videtur quasi ex maleficio te-
neri, & in quantum de ea re aequum religioni judi-
cantis videbitur, poenam sustinebit. in prin.inst eod.
Secudo,is,ex cujus coenaculo, vel proprio ipsius,
vel conducto, vel in quo gratis habitat, dejectum ef-
fusumve aliquid est, ita ut alicui noceret, quasi ex ma-
leficio obligatus intelligitur. §.item is.ex.inst eod.
Tertio,is quasi ex maleficio obligatur, qui ea par-
te, qua vulgò iter fieri solet, id positum aut suspen-
sum habet, quod potest (si ceciderit) alicui nocere,
§.1. verf.cui similis.inst.eod.

de dolo aut furto, quod in navi aut caupona ut sta-

page.notes: The top line is a continuation from the previous page and is set in smaller type; the first word "quando" is printed with a fragment of the line before. The subtitle is in black letter and was transcribed with [?] where the initial "V" of "Von" reads like "B". "aestimaverit" in the continuation line is uncertain (the ligature reads "a(s)timaverit"), so the [?] is placed accordingly. The last word of the final line is cut off by the foot of the page: "co.ü" is a guess at "comitis" and is marked [?]. The printed spellings "Secudo" and "Tertio" are as printed. A dark mark at the bottom centre of the scan is a stain or ink mark, not printed text, and is left out. The large initial "Q" of "Quatuor" is joined to the word. No catchword or signature is printed.
